titre: Prise en charge des tendinopathies rompues de la coiffe des rotateurs : place de la chirurgie
resume: Notes factuelles (démonstration, pas le texte original). Recommandation HAS adoptée par le Collège le 2 juillet 2026, publiée en juillet 2026. Population : adultes avec rupture de la coiffe des rotateurs, traumatique ou dégénérative. Gradation : grades B, C et accord d'experts (AE). Rupture dégénérative : traitement médico-fonctionnel au minimum 6 mois avant de discuter une indication chirurgicale si gêne ou douleur persistent (AE). Une à deux infiltrations cortisonées espacées d'au minimum 3 semaines (grade B). Au moins 1 mois entre la dernière infiltration et la chirurgie (grade C). Rupture traumatique sur tendon sain : avis chirurgical sans délai (grade C). Âge non exclusif : patient actif de plus de 75 ans peut bénéficier de la chirurgie, risque de rupture itérative plus élevé (grade C). Rupture partielle à considérer si plus de 50 % de l'épaisseur. Réparation anatomique de référence, le plus souvent arthroscopique (AE) ; double rang recommandé à long terme, gain préservé à 10 ans (grade C) ; simple rang pour lésions de moins de 3 cm (AE). Acromioplastie non systématique (grade B). Kinésithérapie préopératoire conseillée (AE). Attelle postopératoire 4 à 6 semaines sans immobilisation stricte (grade C). Auto-rééducation prépondérante jusqu'au 3e mois (AE). Reprise des activités quotidiennes à partir du 3e mois, reprise professionnelle, sportive ou de loisirs entre 3 et 6 mois, réathlétisation à partir de 6 mois, récupération habituelle à un an (AE). Ondes de choc contre-indiquées en postopératoire (AE). Pas d'imagerie postopératoire systématique avant 3 mois ; IRM non utile avant 6 mois (AE).

titre: Efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid compared with sham for midportion Achilles tendinopathy (Inject trial): randomised controlled trial
resume: Factual notes (demonstration, not the original abstract). Single-centre, three-arm randomised controlled trial, participants and assessors masked, community setting. 192 adults aged 18 or older with midportion Achilles tendinopathy, randomised 1:1:1 to sham (n=64), high volume injection without corticosteroid (n=63) or with corticosteroid (n=65); enrolment December 2019 to July 2022. Sham: small volume of local anaesthetic. Active arms: large volume saline and bupivacaine, with or without hydrocortisone. All participants received the same exercise programme, education and activity advice. Primary outcome: pain and disability (VISA-A) at 52 weeks. Economic outcome: cost per QALY, societal perspective. Follow-up 6, 26 and 52 weeks. VISA-A available for 94% of participants at 12 months. No clear differences between sham and either injection, or between injections, at 12 months. Corticosteroid injection better than sham at 6 weeks but worse than injection without corticosteroid at 26 weeks. Corticosteroid arm estimated less costly than sham with similar effectiveness. No serious trial related adverse events. Authors: data do not support routine use of high volume corticosteroid injection. Registration ACTRN12619001455156.

titre: Exercise to reduce falls in Community-Dwelling people after stroke: A systematic review with meta-analysis
resume: Factual notes (demonstration, not the original abstract). Systematic review with meta-analysis of randomised trials, published online 24 April 2026. Three randomised trials, 677 participants, community-dwelling people after stroke. Falls prevention exercise versus no or sham intervention. Rate of falls: IRR 0.84 (95% CI 0.62 to 1.15), not statistically significant. Proportion of fallers: RR 0.98 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.18). Balance: non significant trend toward improvement. Preferred walking speed: small significant improvement, 0.04 m/s (95% CI 0.01 to 0.07).

titre: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Combined with Speech-Language Therapy for Post-Stroke Aphasia Recovery: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis
resume: Factual notes (demonstration, not the original abstract). Systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis of RCTs (PRISMA-NMA, PROSPERO CRD42024602404), searches to 24 January 2026. 26 RCTs, 1,136 patients, sample sizes 28 to 96. Interventions: LF-rTMS, LF-rTMS+SLT, LF-rTMS+music+SLT, dual-hemisphere rTMS+SLT, iTBS+SLT, cTBS+SLT; comparators SLT alone or sham TMS+SLT. Seven immediate and four long-term language domains; SMD with 95% credible intervals. Immediate: aphasia severity, LF-rTMS+music+SLT vs SLT SMD 2.05 (0.84 to 3.29); naming SMD 1.96 (1.15 to 2.76); comprehension, dual-rTMS+SLT SMD 1.18 (0.77 to 1.57); functional communication, dual-rTMS+SLT SMD 0.62 (0.06 to 1.17); writing, LF-rTMS+SLT SMD 0.34 (0.10 to 0.58). Long-term: aphasia severity, dual-rTMS+SLT vs SLT SMD 1.23 (0.10 to 2.36), low certainty. RoB 2.0: 18 studies low risk, 5 some concerns, 3 high risk. GRADE: moderate to high certainty for standard comparisons such as LF-rTMS+SLT vs SLT; low to very low for novel combinations. Adverse events mostly headache, dizziness; seizure in two participants in one trial; no serious adverse events. Possible publication bias. Authors: best protocol depends on domain and time point; findings uncertain; head-to-head trials needed.
